channel.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life
channel.description: The latest Essex news, sport and life, updated through the day.

image.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life

item.title: Stansted's Meet the Buyers event turns 25 as local firms chase airport contracts
item.description: London Stansted's networking day for small Essex and East of England suppliers marks a quarter of a century this week.

item.title: Colchester bus gate switched off to ease traffic around St Botolph's Circus works
item.description: Colchester drivers can use a city centre bus gate for now, after it was suspended to relieve congestion caused by the St Botolph's Circus roadworks, the Daily Gazette reports.

item.title: Brentwood residents earn the most in Essex and rank fourth in the UK for pay
item.description: Full-time workers living in Brentwood borough had median pay of £58,540 a year in April 2026, Office for National Statistics figures show, a rise of 16.9% on a year earlier.

item.title: Two teenagers deny murdering Radwan Shakur, 21, in Chelmsford's Central Park
item.description: Jurors in Chelmsford have been told the prosecution case is that the fatal stabbing in the city park in June grew out of a dispute between drug dealers over territory.

item.title: Essex skipper Grace Scrivens to lead England Women A in four-day match in Mumbai
item.description: The Essex Women's captain will take charge of England's second string for the red-ball game that closes their tour of India.

item.title: Flooding partly blocks Axial Way in Colchester during heavy rain
item.description: Torrential rain left part of Axial Way in Colchester under water on the afternoon of Tuesday 17 November, partly blocking the route for drivers.

item.title: University of Essex scientist using AI to spot skin cancer named one of UK's top 50 innovators
item.description: Dr Haider Raza helped build a tool that judges whether a suspicious mole needs a closer look, with the aim of cutting waiting times.

item.title: Aveley crossing patrol officer passes 39 years as Thurrock tells drivers stop means stop
item.description: Thurrock Council is backing the regional Stop Means Stop road safety campaign, with its school crossing patrol officers wearing campaign tabards to remind drivers they must halt when told.

item.title: Tilbury youth zone says youth work must be part of the answer to young people out of work
item.description: OnSide Youth Zone Thames Gateway, due to open in Tilbury in 2027, has responded to Alan Milburn's report on the national crisis of young people not in education, employment or training.

item.title: Underfloor heating firm's founders join Little Havens' corporate supporters after 18 years of giving
item.description: Three business partners behind Fastwarm have pledged £10,800 a year to Little Havens children's hospice in Thundersley, Havens Hospices says.

item.title: Lloyd Scott, who walked the London Marathon in a diving suit, has died
item.description: Tributes have been paid to the former Leyton Orient goalkeeper and firefighter whose costumed marathons raised money for charity, the BBC reports.

item.title: Working-age Tendring households could backdate council tax help by three months
item.description: Tendring District Council wants people of working age who are eligible for its council tax support to be able to claim it for the months before they applied, as pensioners already can.

item.title: Round-the-clock bleed control cabinet unveiled in Chadwell St Mary in memory of Liam Taylor
item.description: A public emergency kit for catastrophic bleeding is now available at all hours in Thurrock, with four more promised for Grays and the Southend area.

item.title: Gemma Collins takes new theatre tour to Southend's Cliffs Pavilion
item.description: The Essex reality TV star has included a night at the Cliffs Pavilion in Southend in a UK theatre tour announced after her latest Sky series, the Echo reports.

item.title: Basildon community station Gateway 97.8's Johnny Jenkins makes Audio Academy 30 Under 30
item.description: A director of Basildon's community radio station, who started there on work experience at 14, has been named among the UK's 30 most promising people in audio under 30.

item.title: c2c trains stopped between Leigh and Shoeburyness after a person dies on the line near Chalkwell
item.description: Rail passengers in Southend and south Essex faced a second round of disruption in a single day, with tickets accepted on other routes while emergency services worked at the scene.

item.title: Woman in her 80s seriously hurt after being hit by a car on Harwich High Street
item.description: Essex Police are asking for dashcam and CCTV footage after a pedestrian was struck near the Park Road junction in Harwich on Saturday 14 November.

item.title: Power cut hits hundreds near Colchester after high-voltage line fault
item.description: A fault on a high-voltage line left hundreds of properties near Colchester without electricity on the morning of Tuesday 17 November.

item.title: Epping Forest MP Neil Hudson presses for easier Blue Badges for people with Parkinson's
item.description: Dr Neil Hudson, MP for Epping Forest, has asked Essex County Council and the Department for Transport to change how people with Parkinson's are assessed for Blue Badges, backing a Parkinson's UK campaign.

item.title: James Blunt booked to top the bill at Colchester Castle Summer Series
item.description: The singer will headline Castle Park, Colchester, on 28 August 2027, with Starsailor and Noonzy also on the line-up, the Echo reports.

item.title: A12 southbound near Ingatestone to stay shut overnight into Wednesday after road collapse
item.description: Drivers heading south through Essex towards Brentwood face a second day of diversions on the B1002 after the carriageway broke apart, with a water leak reported as the cause.

item.title: Former Billericay Town youngster Max Dowman becomes England Under-21s' youngest ever scorer
item.description: Arsenal's Max Dowman, who played for Billericay Town as a boy, scored against France at 16 years and 320 days to beat a record held by Jude Bellingham.

item.title: Former BT transformation director joins Harwich Haven Authority board
item.description: Harwich Haven Authority, the trust port that manages shipping channels into Harwich and Felixstowe, has named Clive Quantrill as a non-executive director.

item.title: Young jobless claimants in Brentwood reach highest level since early 2022
item.description: In Brentwood, 225 people aged 18 to 24 were on the claimant count in October 2026, up 18.4% on a year earlier and roughly double the rise across England.

item.title: Southend drivers get four days of free council parking in the run-up to Christmas
item.description: Southend City Council is bringing back free festive parking to help shops in the city through the Christmas season.

item.title: Knife crime in Essex down by more than a quarter since 2019, violence unit says in Sceptre Week
item.description: Essex's Violence and Vulnerability Unit is pointing to youth projects in Harlow, Chelmsford, Thurrock and south Essex schools as national knife crime week runs.

item.title: Weekly market to come back to Harlow's rebuilt Market Square in February
item.description: Harlow Council is asking traders to come forward to help shape a regular market selling fresh food and gifts in the town centre square.

item.title: Basildon loses 32 planned affordable homes after council agrees changes to two housing schemes
item.description: Basildon Council has let developers in Great Burstead and Basildon town centre cut the affordable housing they had promised, citing rising build costs.

item.title: Basildon sets aside £150,000 for two years of town centre safety wardens
item.description: Basildon Council wants a contractor patrolling the town centre by February 2027, paid for with money from developers.

item.title: Leeds private equity firm Endless takes control of Essex housebuilder Weston Homes
item.description: Essex housebuilder Weston Homes has been bought by private equity firm Endless, ending almost 40 years of ownership led by its founder Bob Weston.

item.title: Fun Walk Trust shares record £123,107 among 62 Essex good causes
item.description: Charities, schools, churches and community groups from Billericay, Brentwood and beyond collected their cheques at the trust's 25th anniversary celebration.

item.title: Heavy bone picked up on Tollesbury sea wall may be from an Ice Age woolly rhino
item.description: A walker's find on the edge of the River Blackwater near Tollesbury could be part of a woolly rhinoceros pelvis, Natural History Museum experts believe.

item.title: West Essex food charity TouchPoint faces hard times despite King's award
item.description: TouchPoint, which gives free food to hundreds of people in west Essex, is going through a difficult spell even after being honoured with a King's award, BBC Essex reports.

item.title: Ex-Thurrock finance chief Sean Clark tells BBC reporter to "go away" over council collapse
item.description: The former finance director behind Thurrock Council's borrowing refused to answer questions about the borough's lost millions, a day after the BBC traced solar businessman Liam Kavanagh to Bucharest.

item.title: Just Ride Southend volunteers win the King's Award for Voluntary Service
item.description: The volunteer-run group in Southend-on-Sea has been given the King's Award for Voluntary Service for 2026, the highest honour for local voluntary groups, SAVS Southend says.

item.title: Colchester City Council answers drivers' complaints over Christmas lights night traffic
item.description: Colchester City Council has replied to complaints from motorists who sat in traffic for hours around the city's Christmas lights switch-on, a jam some residents called horrendous.

item.title: Isthmian Premier: Brentwood Town beaten 3-0 by Ramsgate as Stanway Rovers hold Lewes
item.description: Three first-half goals left the Brentwood side nineteenth in the Isthmian League Premier Division, while the Colchester-area club kept a second clean sheet in a row away in Sussex.

item.title: Wet and windy start to Tuesday across Essex, with gusts close to 40mph
item.description: Rain swept across the county overnight before the wind peaked during the morning, with brighter weather forecast for Wednesday.

item.title: Missing Grays pensioner Patrick Francisco, 83, has been found
item.description: Essex Police shared the good news on Monday night, a few hours after launching an urgent search for him.

item.title: Three vehicles involved in crash that shut Colchester's Chitts Hill
item.description: The road on the edge of Colchester was closed on the evening of Monday 16 November after the collision, and Essex Police asked drivers to avoid the area.

item.title: Police charge man over string of shoplifting offences in Braintree
item.description: Essex Police said on Monday 16 November that a man has been charged with 21 counts of shop theft in Braintree. He has not been convicted of any offence.

item.title: Braintree man, 38, charged with 21 shop thefts in Braintree and Great Notley
item.description: Graham Pink, of Telford Road, Braintree, is due before Chelmsford Crown Court in December after appearing before magistrates.

item.title: More police patrols promised for Corringham town centre after complaints of anti-social behaviour
item.description: Thurrock's divisional police commander has told local councillors officers will be more visible in Corringham, Thurrock Nub News reports.

item.title: Colchester councillors to weigh up major spending plan for Leisure World
item.description: Colchester City Council leaders are taking plans to the council's cabinet for what they call the biggest investment in Leisure World for a generation.

item.title: Three taxis taken off the road after police checks at Harlow station
item.description: Officers in Harlow stopped 62 taxis and private hire vehicles at the railway station and found most of them in order.

item.title: Essex pupils to shape year-long county push against bullying
item.description: Essex County Council has launched Let's Talk... Safe Relationships across Essex, built with the Young Essex Assembly and the Multi-Schools Council.

item.title: Gilston planners tell Epping Forest audience the 10,000-home scheme next to Harlow is a 30-year job
item.description: East Herts Council officers leading the Gilston Area beside Harlow shared lessons on trust, governance and long memories with planners from across the East of England.

item.title: Rosie the Jack Russell is dug out of a Maldon rabbit hole and learns absolutely nothing
item.description: Firefighters cleared trees and dug with great care to free the terrier, who bolted for the next burrow the moment she was out.

item.title: Spanish fashion chain Mango heading for Chelmsford's High Chelmer centre
item.description: Mango plans a new store in the High Chelmer shopping centre in Chelmsford city centre, the Daily Gazette reports.

item.title: Lung cancer screening arrives in Harlow, the first town in west Essex to get it
item.description: Current and former smokers in Harlow are being invited for free checks that can find the disease before any symptoms appear, NHS Essex says.

item.title: Power back on in Chelmer Village and Springfield after underground cable fault
item.description: UK Power Networks reconnected the last homes by 5pm, after a high voltage fault left part of east Chelmsford without electricity for about three hours.

item.title: Police concerned for missing Clacton girl Hannah Steer, 15
item.description: She has not been seen since about 9.30pm on Sunday, and Essex Police says officers need to find her to make sure she is ok.

item.title: Free parking returns to selected Southend council car parks in December
item.description: Southend-on-Sea City Council is waiving charges in nine of its own car parks on four December days to bring shoppers into local high streets.

item.title: St Luke's Hospice bistro launches its first Christmas menu
item.description: SEASONS @ St Luke's, the hospice bistro created with MasterChef finalist Anurag Aggarwal, serves festive meals on weekdays from 1 to 24 December.

item.title: Essex council shake-up still under review as county leaders warn ministers
item.description: The body that speaks for England's county councils says trust in the reorganisation process in Essex and other two-tier areas is at risk.

item.title: Havens Hospices asks Essex to back its Big Yes! Christmas appeal
item.description: The charity that runs Fair Havens and Little Havens Children's Hospice says £31 could pay for an hour of specialist nursing care over Christmas.

item.title: Orsett Hospital clinics moved out before winter as heating fails
item.description: X-ray, orthopaedic and ear, nose and throat services are leaving the ageing Thurrock hospital, and there is no new home yet for its eye and kidney clinics.

item.title: Alresford bowel cancer survivor walks 45 miles for research
item.description: Nina Murton from Alresford, diagnosed with bowel cancer in 2016, has raised almost £600 for the Bowelbabe Fund for Cancer Research UK, walking mostly along the creek to Wivenhoe in October.

item.title: Thurrock Council widens pest checks on Purfleet's Garrison Estate after family forced out by rodents
item.description: Thurrock Council says it is determined to find the root cause of an infestation that drove a woman, her daughter and granddaughter from their council home in Purfleet.

item.title: Colchester Local Plan heads for the inspector after more than 1,800 responses
item.description: Colchester City Council's draft Local Plan, which sets where new homes and jobs go across the city, could be sent for independent examination once a committee reviews the public's comments.
